Court No. - 47  HON'BLE SIDDHARTH, J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A for the State.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today by counsel for the applicant is taken on record.
This is second bail application of the applicant.
First bail application of the applicant was rejected by this court on 22.04.2025.

Counsel for the applicant has brought on record the statement of the victim recorded as P.W.-1 before the trial court wherein she has stated that there is only one door in her house and there is no other door for entry and exit in her house from which anyone can enter or exit from her house.
In the night she sleeps after opening the only door and it remains open for the whole night.
The name of applicant's brother is Bhura.

She has admitted that Bhura lodged F.I.R on 20.03.2023 as Case Crime No. 176 of 2023, under Sections- 452, 323, 504, 506 and 354 IPC and she is appearing as witness against the applicant, Rizwan, in another case lodged by her on 29.04.2023.

She has further stated that at the time when the applicant entered into her house and committed the alleged offence,
her mother-in-law, Jethani and Nanad, were present.
She was present on the second floor of the house where the incident was caused by the applicant.

Counsel for the applicant submits that it is clear from the above that the incident cannot be committed by the applicant after entering into the house of victim where three female members apart from victim and her children were present and she never raised any alarm or cried for help from anyone.
He has further submitted that when only female members were present in the house why they were sleeping in the house after opening the only door of their house in the night has not been explained.
The conduct of the victim is not natural.

He has further pointed out to F.S.L report where from it is clear that the source from which the alleged incriminating videos were sent on the mobile phones of the relatives of victim could not be ascertained by the expert.
Counsel for the applicant also submits that it is clear case of false implication.
The applicant is in jail since 13.06.2024.
On the other hand counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A have opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the above facts on record.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties noted above, finding force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India, considering Rizwan vs State Of U.P. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177524997/
2 the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 LawSuit (SC) 677 and considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by the under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Rizwan, involved in Case Crime No. 249 of 2023, under Sections- 452, 354,
376(2)N, 323, 506 IPC and Section 67 of I.T. Act, Police Station- Izzatnagar, District- Bareilly, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or as directed by the Court.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence,
proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i)
opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case, of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
Trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the applicant as expeditiously as possible preferably within period of six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
(Siddharth,J.) September 8, 2025 Rohit  Rizwan vs State Of U.P. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177524997/
